summary: The extension to nodes 1, 2 and 5 changes the severity of the finding. Those three nodes each report accepted 38 and decided 38 with a StopSign at index 37, while nodes 3 and 4 report accepted 37 with the StopSign at index 36 and nothing at index 37. The same reconfiguration marker therefore sits one index later in one group, so the logs genuinely diverge at index 36 and the two groups hold different numbers of preceding entries. Node 4 is decided 38 while holding only 37 positions, which handle_accepted permits by taking a follower-reported accepted index from the longer group once is_chosen counts a quorum. Node 3, decided 37 with accepted 37, receives the Decides as its next expected messages, clamps decided, sends no PrepareReq, is offered no AcceptStopSign because it already accepted one, and stays behind for the whole window. The update records the divergent marker placement as a new fact, revises the hypothesis from a local progress gap to a divergent log layout that a leader then decides past, and restates the interpretation as both a safety-relevant divergence and a progress loss. It also states explicitly that the earlier zero divergence count was an artifact of the comparison helper, which ignores StopSign entries and prefix length, and notes that index 36 on nodes 1, 2 and 5 was not read directly. No execution is requested.
